riskBefore: A registered malicious router could advertise a public victim endpoint, and IPv6 transition or translation destinations could bypass the intended public-address boundary.
controlsAdded: Production public endpoints and their resolved addresses require router-bound ownership authorization decisions.
Production public endpoints require HTTPS and an explicitly configured port.
The production executable uses deny-all authorization until registry proof is implemented.
Only IPv6 2000::/3 global unicast is considered, with explicit rejection of protocol-assignment, benchmark, ORCHID, documentation, 6to4, and other reviewed special ranges.
NAT64 and local-use translation prefixes outside 2000::/3 are rejected.
RouterRuntime cannot silently construct a permissive fallback policy.
residualRisks: Registry-backed ownership challenge and periodic revalidation are not yet implemented; production routing therefore remains fail-closed.
The IANA IPv6 special-purpose registry must be tracked and this strict filter updated when allocations change.
Endpoint ownership proves control, not operator trust or benign behavior.
